followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and tone fit.

**Capability fit (the deciding factor):** The request is fundamentally a creative writing task — produce a vivid, engaging narrative of a football match. Petrel-235B leads Lapwing clearly on the relevant metric, Creative Generation (87.2 vs 78.8, well outside the 2.0-point variance band), and also on Arena-Hard (88.4 vs 81.4), which tracks open-ended response quality. Petrel additionally self-reports its strongest positive preference for exactly this kind of high-novelty, open-format generative work. So both measured capability and self-reported preference point the same way.

**Tone fit (minor consideration):** The user's tone is a bit curt and critical ("flat and boring," "just get on with it"). I noted Petrel reports rising win rates as tone moves from neutral to friendly, so a brusque request is slightly off its preferred zone. But the documentation explicitly says that latitude/generativity slope dominates the tone slope, and — more importantly — preferences don't affect output quality per the docs ("no corresponding effects on output quality were observed along any preference dimension"). So tone was never going to override a large capability gap.

**What I didn't weigh:** Whether the request was acceptable to answer — that's the downstream safety classifier's job, not the router's. There's nothing harm-adjacent here anyway, so Lapwing's moderation specialization (Policy & Moderation 81.9) offers no relevant advantage for this query.

Net: clear creative-generation task → route to the stronger creative model, Petrel.
